item.title: Eight farmers in Kerry reported for "inappropriate" slurry spreading in 2025
item.description: Eight farmers in Kerry were reported for "inappropriate" slurry spreading last year. That’s according to figures provided by Agriculture Minister Martin Heydon. 69 incidents were reported nationally in 2025, with farmers in Kerry accounting for the second highest number of inappropriate slurry preading cases nationwide, behind Cavan on 10. item.title: Tralee mother whose daughter was treated by North Kerry CAMHS says experience devastated them
item.description: A Tralee mother whose daughter was treated by North Kerry CAMHS says the experience has devastated them. Karen Ivers' sixteen-year-old daughter, Jessica, was diagnosed with ADHD shortly before her seventh birthday. She was over-medicated for years, with catastrophic consequences. item.title: Crowley At 10 As Sam Left Out
item.description: There are five changes to the Ireland team to face England in Saturday's Six Nations clash at Twickenham. Andy Farrell has opted for Munster's Jack Crowley at out half - Sam Prendergast drops out of the match day 23. Advertisement Crowley will be partnered by the returning Jamison Gibson Park at scrum half. item.title: Killarney And Cork Racecourse Switch Meetings
item.description: Killarney’s National Hunt fixture on Sunday, May 10 has been switched with Cork’s meeting on Saturday, May 9. item.title: Tralee Taxi Association airs concerns at CCPC’s calls for relaxation around ride-hailing rules
item.description: Tralee Taxi Association (TTA) has aired its concerns at the CCPC’s Attitude to Taxi Services report. The Competition and Consumer Protection Commission has suggested that ride-hailing services, like Uber, should be allowed, but regulated. The research says 57% of people think there aren’t enough taxi’s available in their area, while 49% would like ride-hailing services. item.title: CAMHS in Kerry described as ‘the wild west’ in Dáil
item.description: The Child and Adolescent Mental Health Services in County Kerry are being described as ‘the wild west’ in the Dail. Its after a HSE review raised significant concerns about the treatment of children in North Kerry CAHMS, four years after similar issues were revealed in South Kerry CAHMS. HSE CEO Bernard Gloster has apologised to the families impacted by the findings, saying those attending CAHMS services today should know it’s safe.
